tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

	t.Parallel()

	r := testutil.NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()
	good := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "good")
	r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", nil)
	rogue := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "rogue")
	rogueEntry := r.Record(r.Rogue, "refs/heads/main", nil)
	r.Annotate(r.Cluster, true, "revoked", rogueEntry)

	// gittuf accepts a fix tree-same with the last good state, here one that
	// keeps the rogue commit as its parent.
	goodTree, err := r.Git.GetCommitTreeID(good)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	out, err := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "git", "-C", r.Dir, "commit-tree", goodTree.String(), "-p", rogue.String(), "-m", "fix").CombinedOutput()

	fix, err := githash.NewHash(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	r.SetRef("refs/heads/main", fix)
	r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", nil)

	atFix := run(t.Context(), t, r.Dir, "refs/heads/main", time.Minute)
	require.Equal(t, Verified, atFix.State, "%s: %v", atFix.Reason, atFix.Err)

	r.SetRef("refs/heads/main", rogue)
	atRogue := run(t.Context(), t, r.Dir, "refs/heads/main", time.Minute)

	assert.Equal(t, Failed, atRogue.State)
	tip := checkByName(t, atRogue, CheckTip)
	assert.Equal(t, CheckFail, tip.Status)
	assert.Contains(t, tip.Detail, "brought in by skipped entry")
}

package testutil

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/githash"

)

// Fixture checkpoint IDs. CheckpointULID's shard is "7Z" and CheckpointHex's
// is "f7", the last two characters of each.
const (
	CheckpointULID = "01JC0FFEE0BADC0DE00000007Z"
	CheckpointHex  = "a3b2c4d5e6f7"
	RepositoryID   = "01J9ZREPQ0000000000000000R"
	PusherJane     = "01J9ZACCT000000000000000JD (jane)"
	PusherBob      = "01J9ZACCT000000000000000BB (bob)"
)

// Scenario is a repository shaped like one Entire's server records: a root
// of trust authorizing the cluster key, branches, a moved tag, checkpoint refs,
// a rogue entry and a revoked one.
type Scenario struct {
	*Repo

	MainFirst, MainSecond         githash.Hash // commits on main
	MainFirstEntry, MainLastEntry githash.Hash // RSL entries for main
	TrailerCommit                 githash.Hash // main tip, carries Entire-Checkpoint
	FeatureEntry                  githash.Hash // recorded by the mirror service
	TagFirstEntry, TagMovedEntry  githash.Hash // v1.0.0 recorded twice
	CheckpointEntry               githash.Hash // refs/entire/checkpoints/7Z/<ULID>
	RogueEntry                    githash.Hash // refs/heads/rogue, signed by Rogue
	FixedGoodEntry                githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, first and valid
	RevokedCommit                 githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, only the skipped entry brought it in
	RevokedEntry, RevokeAnnot     githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, rogue and skipped
	FixedEntry                    githash.Hash // refs/heads/fixed, the fix back to the good state
}

// CheckpointRef returns the git-refs backend ref for a checkpoint ID.
func CheckpointRef(id string) string {
	return "refs/entire/checkpoints/" + id[len(id)-2:] + "/" + id
}

func pushedBy(pusher string, extra ...string) rsl.CustomFields {
	fields := rsl.CustomFields{
		"custom.entire.io/repository": RepositoryID,
		"custom.entire.io/pusher":     pusher,
	}
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(extra); i += 2 {
		fields[extra[i]] = extra[i+1]
	}
	return fields
}

content.text:
I fixed two of the three. The worktree-config finding is a false positive, so I only added a regression test for it. Format, lint (golangci-lint 2.15.0, the version mise pins) and `go test -race ./...` all pass. I ran those steps by hand because `mise.toml` isn't trusted here.

**Windows test failure.** Git for Windows runs `core.alternateRefsCommand` through `sh`, which treats the backslashes in `C:\Users\...\marker` as escape characters. So `touch` created a file with a different name and the marker never appeared. I changed the command to `touch '<filepath.ToSlash(marker)>'; true` in `internal/gitcli/config_test.go:205`. I made the same change in `cmd/entire-rsl/cli/fetch_test.go:80`, which had the same bug but only asserts `NoFileExists`, so it passed on Windows without proving anything. I haven't run either test on Windows, so this needs a CI run to confirm.

**Good ancestors marked revoked: confirmed, fixed.** I reproduced it in `TestRevokedCommitKeptByARecoveryCommitFailsVerification`: a `base` commit pushed in an unskipped entry before the rogue push came back as `failed` ("brought in by skipped entry #4"). Now `relateBehind` (`internal/tipstate/tipstate.go:153`) first finds the oldest unskipped push that contains the commit. A skipped entry revokes the commit only if it is older than that push. The rogue commit is still `revoked` and `base` now verifies. Two behaviour notes:
- A commit both revoked and more than 1000 entries back now shows as `too_far` instead of `revoked`. Neither verifies.
- The search for the oldest push stops at the first entry that doesn't contain the commit, such as one before a force push. So a skipped entry between that break and an older unskipped push still marks the commit revoked. That errs toward failing.

**Worktree config ignores common dir: false positive.** go-git's `RepositoryFilesystem` sends `config` to the common dir and `config.worktree` to `.git/worktrees/<name>` (`storage/filesystem/dotgit/repository_filesystem.go:66` in go-git v6.0.0-beta.1). So `rawConfig` already reads both from the right places. I added `TestLookupConfigInLinkedWorktree`, which checks shared and worktree-only keys against `git config --get`. It passes on the current code and would catch a regression if go-git changed this.

Proposed commits, each ending with `Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` then `Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>`, and signed as your memory note says:

1. `tipstate: revoke only commits a skipped push brought in first` (`internal/tipstate/tipstate.go`, `internal/verify/verify_test.go`)
2. `test: pass the alternateRefsCommand marker as a shell-safe path` (`internal/gitcli/config_test.go`, `cmd/entire-rsl/cli/fetch_test.go`)
3. `store: test config lookup from a linked worktree` (`internal/store/store_test.go`)

Should I commit them on `general-improvements`?

  includes, see "The fetch allows only known repository config"); output is

  read, and include files are not followed. Only the `local` and `worktree`
  scopes are checked. Global and system config are the user's own, and the
  `command` scope holds entire-rsl's overrides. Allowed: `core`
  `repositoryformatversion`, `filemode`, `bare`, `logallrefupdates`,
  `ignorecase`, `precomposeunicode`, `symlinks`; `extensions.objectformat`,
  `refstorage` and `worktreeconfig`; `remote.<name>` `url`, `pushurl`, `fetch`, `push`,
  `tagopt`, `mirror`, `prune`, `prunetags`, `promisor`,
  `partialclonefilter`, `entiredb-original-url`; every `branch.<name>` key,
  since git reads them only to pick upstreams and editors add their own;
  `user.name`, `email`, `signingkey`; `commit.gpgsign`, `tag.gpgsign`;
  `gpg.format`. The list was built from the `.git/config` of every
  repository under entireio. Any other key, or a listed key without the
  subsection its section needs, refuses the fetch with every offending key
  named once, sanitized, in git's order. Values are never shown. A failure
  to list the config is an error and nothing is fetched. There is no
  override: the user can fetch the gittuf refs with git.
- **Defence in depth:** the runner also passes `-c core.alternateRefsCommand=`,
  which a test shows makes git list an alternate's refs itself.
- **Per-worktree config:** `extensions.worktreeConfig` is allowed. It only
  makes git read `config.worktree`, whose keys are listed in the `worktree`
  scope and checked against the same allowlist.
- **Rejected:** extending the denylist, and an override flag.

package testutil

import (
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/policy"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/rsl"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	IsolateGitConfig()
	os.Exit(m.Run())
}

func TestFixtureVerifiesWithGittuf(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()

	commit := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "first")
	entry := r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", rsl.CustomFields{"custom.entire.io/pusher": "01J9ZAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA (jane)"})

	tip, err := policy.VerifyRef(t.Context(), r.Git, "refs/heads/main")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, commit, tip)

	got, err := rsl.GetEntry(r.Git, entry)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	refEntry, ok := got.(*rsl.ReferenceEntry)
	require.True(t, ok)
	value, ok := refEntry.GetCustomField("custom.entire.io/pusher")
	require.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, "01J9ZAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA (jane)", value)
}

func TestFixtureRogueSignatureFailsGittuf(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()
	r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "first")
	r.Record(r.Rogue, "refs/heads/main", nil)

	_, err := policy.VerifyRef(t.Context(), r.Git, "refs/heads/main")
	require.Error(t, err)
}

func TestFixtureIsDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	build := func() string {
		r := NewRepo(t)
		r.Bootstrap()
		r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "first")
		return r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", nil).String()
	}

  repository's own config could point the remote at a local path, `file://`,
  ssh or scp-like syntax, `git://`, plain `http://`, or another remote

  through the Entire CLI's remote helper.

The check is in place and format, lint, `go test -race ./...` and `go mod tidy` are all clean. I haven't committed yet: your instructions say to show the commit first, and signing needs a key touch.

**The check** (`internal/gitcli/config.go`): before a fetch, `CheckFetchConfig` refuses any `remote.<name>.url` in `.git/config` or `config.worktree` that doesn't start with `https://` or `entire://`. That covers local paths, `file://`, ssh, scp-like `git@host:repo`, `git://`, `http://` and remote helpers such as `fd::` and `ext::`.
- It checks every remote, not only the one being fetched, and a `url` key with no value is refused too.
- The match is case-sensitive, so `HTTPS://` is refused. git chooses the transport by the scheme exactly as written, so this fails closed.
- The error names the key, e.g. `remote.origin.url (not an https:// or entire:// URL)`. It never prints the URL, since URLs can hold credentials.
- `pushurl` isn't checked because a fetch never uses it. Say if you want it included.

**Test harness change:** many CLI tests cloned and fetched from local paths, which are now refused.
- `testutil.IsolateGitConfig` now writes a temporary global config that rewrites `https://local.test/` to `file:///`. It returns a cleanup function, so every `TestMain` changed.
- `Repo.Clone` and the `AddRemote` callers use `testutil.LocalURL(dir)`. Global config is the user's own and isn't checked, so these tests still go through the real fetch path.
- `newClone` in `internal/gitcli` now sets an `https://` origin.

**Tests:**
- New cases in `internal/gitcli` cover refused schemes, the URL never appearing in the error, several remotes, the worktree scope, a key with no value, and accepted `https://` and `entire://` URLs.
- `TestFetchRefusesUnsafeRepositoryConfig` gains cases for a local-path remote and a `file://` remote.

**Docs:** an entry in `docs/decisions.md`, plus one line each in `README.md` and `SECURITY.md`.

Proposed commit (all 15 changed files):

```
gitcli: fetch only from https:// and entire:// remotes

The fetch gate allowed remote.<name>.url with any value, so a
repository's own config could point a remote at a local path, file://,
ssh, git://, plain http:// or another remote helper.

CheckFetchConfig now refuses every remote.<name>.url in the local and
worktree scopes that does not start with https:// or entire://, matched
case-sensitively as git picks the transport by the scheme as written.
The key is named and the URL never shown.

Test fixtures clone from https://local.test/<path>, which the global
config IsolateGitConfig writes rewrites to file:///.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
```
